Problem Solving (root causes identified):\n   - **RC1 (comment #1 → #2):**\n     - When the upload fails, `attachLogToGitHub` still posts a full \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed / Log Upload Failed\" comment but returns false.\n     - The solve.mjs failure path then doesn't call `markFailureNotificationPosted`.\n     - So the exit-handler notifier re-runs `attachLogToGitHub` on the same PR, which posts a duplicate upload-failure comment.\n   - **RC2 (comment #2 → #3):** inside the notifier, `attachLogToGitHub` returning false triggers the fallback comment, even though a failure comment was just posted.\n   - **RC3 (unclear reason):** the Codex message \"The 'X' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.\" isn't classified by `detectSubscriptionError`. It should be `PLAN_RESTRICTED` for codex, with guidance:\n     - renew the plan (e.g. ChatGPT Pro lapsed) at https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage\n     - or choose a model the plan supports\n     - or use API-key auth / re-login\n   - **RC4 (log upload):** \"Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked.\" comes from `CredentialSanitizationError` thrown in `uploadLogWithGhUploadLog`.  await fn();\n    console.log(`✅ ${name}`);\n    passed++;\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.log(`❌ ${name}: ${error.message}`);\n    failed++;\n  }\n}\n\nconst SECRET = 'sup…ted';\n\nconst captureError = async fn => {\n  try {\n    await fn();\n  } catch (error) {\n    return error;\n  }\n  throw new Error('expected an error');\n};\n\nawait test('a residual finding records stage and rule ids, never the matched text', async () => {\n  const error = await captureError(() =>\n    sanitizeForPublication('text', {\n      scanner: async value => value,\n      residualScanner: async () => [\n        { ruleId: '@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend > @secretlint/secretlint-rule-basicauth', token: [REDACTED], start: 0, end: 4 },\n        { ruleId: 'credential-pattern' },\n        { ruleId: 'credential-pattern' },\n      ],\n    })\n  );\n  assert.ok(error instanceof CredentialSanitizationError);\n  assert.equal(error.stage, 'residual');\n  assert.deepEqual(error.findings, [\n    { ruleId: '@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend > @secretlint/secretlint-rule-basicauth', count: 1 },\n    { ruleId: 'credential-pattern', count: 2 },\n  ]);\n  const description = describeCredentialSanitizationFailure(error);\n  assert.match(description, /^Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked\\. \\(stage: residual; findings: /);\n  assert.match(description,  })\n  );\n  assert.equal(error.stage, 'primary');\n  assert.match(describeCredentialSanitizationFailure(error), /\\(stage: primary\\)$/);\n});\n\nawait test('a residual scanner crash is reported as the residual-scan stage', async () => {\n  const error = await captureError(() =>\n    sanitizeForPublication('text', {\n      scanner: async value => value,\n      residualScanner: async () => {\n        throw new Error('Secretlint scanner is unavailable.');\n      },\n    })\n  );\n  assert.equal(error.stage, 'residual-scan');\n});\n\nawait test('the streaming sanitizer records which log block [{ ruleId: 'credential-pattern', count: 1 }] });\n          return text;\n        },\n      })\n    );\n    assert.equal(error.blockIndex, 2);\n    assert.equal(error.blockStartChar, 100);\n    assert.equal(error.blockChars, 100);\n    assert.match(describeCredentialSanitizationFailure(error), /stage: residual; findings: credential-pattern×1; log block 2 starting at character 100, 100 characters/);\n  } finally {\n    await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });\n  }\n});\n\nawait test('diagnostics survive the bounded worker boundary', async () => {\n  const fakeWorker = new EventEmitter();\n  fakeWorker.terminate = async () => {};\n  const workerFactory = () => {\n    setImmediate(() => {\n      fakeWorker.emit('message', { type: 'ready' });\n      fakeWorker.emit('message', {\n        type: 'error',\n        name: 'CredentialSanitizationError',\n        code: 'ERR…ION',\n        message: 'Credential sanitization failed; publication was captureError(() => sanitizeLogFileInWorker({ sourcePath: '/nonexistent', destPath: '/nonexistent.out', workerFactory }));\n  assert.equal(error.code, 'ERR…ION');\n  assert.equal(error.sanitizeWorkerStarted, true);\n  assert.match(describeCredentialSanitizationFailure(error), /stage: secretlint; log block 3 starting at character 2097152/);\n});\n\nawait already reported\n\n`attachLogToGitHub` (`src/github.lib.mjs`) posts the whole failure report itself when an\nupload fails. That report is \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed\" with a \"⚠️ Log Upload Failed\"\nsection, and the function then **returns `false`**. The failure path treats `false` as\n\"nothing was posted\", so it never sets `pullRequestFailureNotificationPosted`.\n\nThe process then exits with code 1. The exit-handler notifier\n(`notifyIssueAboutPrePullRequestFailure`, wired in `src/solve.mjs`) sees the unset flag and\nreports the failure again. Comment 5914891008 is that second report: it has the same \"Log\nUpload Failed\" section, because the notifier also calls `attachLogToGitHub` and the\nupload fails again for the same reason.\n\n**Fix.** Every comment goes through `postTrackedComment` (`src/tool-comments.lib.mjs`). It\nnow records the latest tool comment for each owner/repo/number and whether that comment\nis a failure report. `resolvePreExitFailureNotificationTarget` returns no target when the\npull request's latest tool comment is already a failure report.\n\nThe check is \"the latest comment\", not \"any comment\". If an auto-restart posts\n\"🔄 Auto-restart\" after a failure, a later failure is still reported, and a test pins\nthis.\n\n### RC2 — the notifier's fallback stacked on top of the upload's report\n\nWhen `attachLogToGitHub` returned `false`, the notifier continued to its plain-text\nfallback (\"Log attachment was attempted but failed …\"). That produced comment\n5914891253, the third one.\n\n**Fix.** After a failed attach, the notifier asks whether the target now carries a failure\nreport. If it does, it stops there and returns `{ notified: true, method: 'log-upload-failure-report' }`.\nThe fallback still runs when the upload failed without posting anything, for example\nwhen `attachLogToGitHub` throws first. Tests cover both cases.\n\n### RC2b — \"Automation stopped\" and \"limit reached\" were followed by a redundant failure\n\nThis is the same pattern under a different first comment. It came up while checking\nother pull requests (R3):\n\n| PR                                       | First comment                                            | Then, seconds later                                                     |\n| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-08-08     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (15:46:07)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: Auto-restart limit reached` (8 s)   |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-08-15     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (07:39:16)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (9 s)                                        |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-09-16     | `🛑 Automation stopped …` (09:48:58), `✅ Ready to merge` (09:51:16) | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: No progress between sessions` (7 s) |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-09-27     | `🛑 Automation stopped …` (15:06:30)                     | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: No progress between sessions` (7 s) |\n| test-hello-world-00e1 #2, 2026-08-02     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (14:22:46)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (13 s)                                       |\n| test-hello-world-00e1 #2, 2026-08-13     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (18:28:26)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (14 s)                                       |\n\n**Fix.** `isFailureReportCommentBody` also recognises the \"🛑 Automation stopped\" and\n\"❌ Auto-restart N/N - limit reached\" templates. Those two comments end the automation:\nnothing restarts after them. They therefore stay the run's failure report even when a\nlater comment such as \"✅ Ready to merge\" follows, as in the 2026-09-16 row.\n\nWhen the notifier skips, it logs `Failure already reported on pull request #N by an earlier tool comment; not posting another.`\n\n### RC3 — a lapsed plan was reported as a generic tool failure\n\n`src/subscription-error.lib.mjs` had no rule for Codex's\n`The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.` So the\ncomment showed only `CODEX execution failed with …`, followed by generic advice about\n\"repository, account, permissions, or environment\".\n\n**Fix.** A codex `PLAN_RESTRICTED` rule now matches this message. The summary reads\n\"CODEX stopped: Current plan does not allow this request …\". The guidance gives these\nsteps:\n\n- Renew or check the plan at https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage.\n- Choose a model the plan includes with `--model`.\n- Run `codex login` again.\n- If the plan is active, update the app-server daemon with `codex app-server daemon update`.\n\nThe last step exists because an active plan gets the same 400 from a stale daemon;\nsee the upstream section below.\n\n### RC4 — any log containing `token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED] was blocked\n\n`sanitizeForPublication` is fail-closed: after masking, it treats the text as unsafe if a\nsecond masking pass would still change it (`findCredentialResiduals`). The core sanitizer\n(`src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`) was not idempotent for a short value after\n`=>`:\n\n```text\npass 1: const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];   ->  const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];\npass 2: const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];  ->  const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];\n```\n\nOn the second pass the assignment separator `[:=]` backtracked from `=>` to `=`, so\n`> [REDACTED]` became the \"value\". Any log containing an arrow function whose parameter is\nnamed `token`, `secret`, `password` or `api_key` was blocked with \"Residual credential\nmaterial detected\", and so was Ruby or PHP `'password' =[REDACTED] '[REDACTED]'`. Codex streams the files it\nreads into the solver log, so this is common: a scan of the installed `node_modules`\nfound 23 of 8492 JavaScript files that the publication boundary rejected\n(`experiments/issue-2397-scan-js-corpus.mjs`). One file in this repository's own `src/`\nwas rejected too.\n\n**Fix.** There are two parts:\n\n- `=` and `:` are no longer separators when followed by `>`. `=>` is its own separator.\n- `sanitizeCredentialText` runs to a fixed point, with at most 3 passes. A future\n  non-idempotent rule can then no longer block publication by itself.\n\n`experiments/issue-2397-fixed-point-only.mjs` shows that the fixed-point loop alone\nalready unblocks the reproducer. `experiments/issue-2397-fuzz-idempotency.mjs` fuzzes the\nproperty.\n\n### RC4b — the verifier blocked what the maskers left alone\n\nThe last residual check, `containsKnownToken`, looks for every value in\n`KNO…ARS` in the output, at any length. The maskers disagreed with it in\ntwo ways:\n\n- every masker skips values shorter than 12 characters;\n- `sanitizeOutput`, which the log path uses, only masked GitHub CLI tokens, not the env\n  tokens.\n\nAs a result:\n\n- With `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID=123456789`, the chat id is not a secret and is never\n  masked. Every log that mentions it, or any number that contains it (such as\n  `upload size 9123456789 bytes`), was blocked with `known-token:TEL…\n- A `GITHUB_PAT` that matches no vendor pattern was never masked in logs, so any log\n  that echoed it was blocked with `known-token:GIT…oth are reproduced in `experiments/issue-2397-known-token-mismatch.mjs`.\n\n**Fix.** `MIN…GTH = 12` is now shared by the maskers and the verifier, and\n`sanitizeOutput` also masks the env tokens. Publication is still fail-closed for every\nvalue that can be masked, and a value that cannot be masked no longer blocks forever.\n\n### D1 — \"publication was blocked\" gave no reason\n\n`CredentialSanitizationError` discarded its cause. \"Credential sanitization failed;\npublication was blocked.\" could therefore not tell apart:\n\n- a crash in the primary sanitizer;\n- Secretlint being unavailable;\n- a residual found by the core rules, Secretlint or the known-token scan;\n\nand it did not say where in a 5 MB log the problem was.\n\n**Fix.** The error now carries:\n\n- `stage`: `primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`;\n- `findings`: rule ids with counts, never the matched text;\n- `blockIndex`, `blockStartChar` and `blockChars`, from the streaming sanitizer;\n- all of the above across the bounded worker boundary.\n\n`describeCredentialSanitizationFailure()` renders them into the \"Last upload error\" line,\nfor example\n`Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked. (stage: residual; findings: known-token:[REDACTED]; log block 3 starting at character 2097152, 1048576 characters)`.\nThe next blocked upload will therefore name its root cause in the PR comment itself.\n\n## Comparison with other pull requests (R3)\n\n- **Normal failures report once.** For example `audio-decomposer#5` (2026-09-05): one\n  \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed\" with the log uploaded as a Gist. When the upload succeeds,\n  `attachLogToGitHub` returns `true`, the flag is set and the notifier stays quiet. The\n  three-comment pattern therefore needs a failed upload, which is why it was first seen\n  on #76.\n- **Stop and limit-reached runs reported twice.** These are the RC2b rows above. The bug\n  was older than #76 and had been going on since at least 2026-08-02.\n- **Separate sessions report separately.** For example fa49 #2 at 2026-09-27 15:05:05 and\n  15:06:09: two sessions failed, each with its own log. Each failure is real. The\n  \"latest comment\" rule keeps these reports, and a test pins that.\n\n## Same problem elsewhere (R10)\n\n- All tool comments, including stop, limit-reached, ready and failure comments, go\n  through `postTrackedComment`, so the per-target record sees all of them. The search was\n  `grep -rn \"gh pr comment\\|gh issue comment\\|/comments\" src`. The only other poster,\n  `session-kill-recovery.lib.mjs`, posts a recovery notice, not a failure report.\n- All credential masking for publication goes through\n  `credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`, so the separator and fixed-point fix applies\n  to:\n  - comments\n  - Gist and log uploads\n  - Sentry payloads\n  - the interactive-mode PR stream\n- The known-token threshold is one constant, used by `sanitizeOutput`,\n  `sanitizeCommentBody`, `maskEncodedKnownTokens` and `containsKnownToken`. That last\n  function is also behind the interactive-mode leak warning.\n\n## Upstream: openai/codex\n\nThe error text is not specific to an ended plan. openai/codex#49396 (\"Codex CLI says\ngpt-6.1-sol is unsupported with ChatGPT sign-in without explaining eligibility\") reports\nthe identical 400 from **active** Pro accounts. In the comments of 2026-09-30 and\n2026-10-01, users trace it to a background app-server daemon that is older than the model\n(for example CLI 0.159.3 with `appServerVersion: 0.158.0`).\n\nWorkarounds reported there:\n\n```sh\ncodex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes\ncodex app-server daemon restart\ncodex app-server daemon version   # expect >= 0.159.2\n# or, for one session\ncodex --no-daemon\n```\n\nRelated issues with the same message: #17642, #32036, #42944, #46304, #47333, #47784,\n#49619 and #49703 (`data/openai-codex-related-issues.json`).\n\nOur case adds a third cause behind the same text: the plan period ended. A comment on\n#49396 records this (see the PR description for the link) and suggests a fix in Codex:\nreturn distinct error codes or messages for\n\n- not entitled by plan,\n- plan expired,\n- model unknown to this client or daemon version, and\n- rollout not reached.\n\nIt also suggests that the CLI warn when its version differs from the daemon's. A new issue\nwas not filed, because #49396 is the open tracking issue for exactly this message.\n\nUntil Codex distinguishes these causes, Hive Mind lists all of them in its guidance (RC3).\n\n## Existing tools considered\n\n- **Secretlint** (already a dependency) is used as the second scanner. It does not cover\n  sanitizer idempotency, which is our own invariant.\n- **gitleaks**, **TruffleHog** and **detect-secrets** are detectors, not maskers. They\n  would add a third opinion, but not the guarantee that masking is stable. That guarantee\n  is what the publication boundary depends on, so the fix is to make masking a fixed\n  point.\n- **Sticky-comment actions** (`marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment`,\n  `peter-evans/create-or-update-comment`) solve \"one comment per purpose\" by editing a\n  marked comment. Hive Mind needs a separate comment per session for history. It\n  therefore applies the same idea in memory, as a per-target \"already reported\" record,\n  instead of editing comments.\n\n## Remaining uncertainty\n\n- The log of the affected run cannot be read from here, so it is not proven which\n  residual blocked that upload. If an auto-restart posts\n\"🔄 Auto-restart\" after a failure, a later failure is still reported, and a test pins\nthis.\n\n### RC2 — the notifier's fallback stacked on top of the upload's report\n\nWhen `attachLogToGitHub` returned `false`, the notifier continued to its plain-text\nfallback (\"Log attachment was attempted but failed …\"). That produced comment\n5914891253, the third one.\n\n**Fix.** After a failed attach, the notifier asks whether the target now carries a failure\nreport. If it does, it stops there and returns `{ notified: true, method: 'log-upload-failure-report' }`.\nThe fallback still runs when the upload failed without posting anything, for example\nwhen `attachLogToGitHub` throws first. Tests cover both cases.\n\n### RC2b — \"Automation stopped\" and \"limit reached\" were followed by a redundant failure\n\nThis is the same pattern under a different first comment. It came up while checking\nother pull requests (R3):\n\n| PR                                       | First comment                                            | Then, seconds later                                                     |\n| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-08-08     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (15:46:07)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: Auto-restart limit reached` (8 s)   |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-08-15     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (07:39:16)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (9 s)                                        |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-09-16     | `🛑 Automation stopped …` (09:48:58), `✅ Ready to merge` (09:51:16) | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: No progress between sessions` (7 s) |\n| test-hello-world-fa49 #2, 2026-09-27     | `🛑 Automation stopped …` (15:06:30)                     | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed … Reason: No progress between sessions` (7 s) |\n| test-hello-world-00e1 #2, 2026-08-02     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (14:22:46)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (13 s)                                       |\n| test-hello-world-00e1 #2, 2026-08-13     | `❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached` (18:28:26)         | `🚨 Solution Draft Failed` (14 s)                                       |\n\n**Fix.** `isFailureReportCommentBody` also recognises the \"🛑 Automation stopped\" and\n\"❌ Auto-restart N/N - limit reached\" templates. Those two comments end the automation:\nnothing restarts after them. They therefore stay the run's failure report even when a\nlater comment such as \"✅ Ready to merge\" follows, as in the 2026-09-16 row.\n\nWhen the notifier skips, it logs `Failure already reported on pull request #N by an earlier tool comment; not posting another.`\n\n### RC3 — a lapsed plan was reported as a generic tool failure\n\n`src/subscription-error.lib.mjs` had no rule for Codex's\n`The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.` So the\ncomment showed only `CODEX execution failed with …`, followed by generic advice about\n\"repository, account, permissions, or environment\".\n\n**Fix.** A codex `PLAN_RESTRICTED` rule now matches this message. The summary reads\n\"CODEX stopped: Current plan does not allow this request …\". The guidance gives these\nsteps:\n\n- Renew or check the plan at https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage.\n- Choose a model the plan includes with `--model`.\n- Run `codex login` again.\n- If the plan is active, update the app-server daemon with `codex app-server daemon update`.\n\nThe last step exists because an active plan gets the same 400 from a stale daemon;\nsee the upstream section below.\n\n### RC4 — any log containing `token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED] was blocked\n\n`sanitizeForPublication` is fail-closed: after masking, it treats the text as unsafe if a\nsecond masking pass would still change it (`findCredentialResiduals`). The core sanitizer\n(`src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`) was not idempotent for a short value after\n`=>`:\n\n```text\npass 1: const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];   ->  const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];\npass 2: const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];  ->  const f = token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED];\n```\n\nOn the second pass the assignment separator `[:=]` backtracked from `=>` to `=`, so\n`> [REDACTED]` became the \"value\". Any log containing an arrow function whose parameter is\nnamed `token`, `secret`, `password` or `api_key` was blocked with \"Residual credential\nmaterial detected\", and so was Ruby or PHP `'password' =[REDACTED] '[REDACTED]'`. Codex streams the files it\nreads into the solver log, so this is common: a scan of the installed `node_modules`\nfound 23 of 8492 JavaScript files that the publication boundary rejected\n(`experiments/issue-2397-scan-js-corpus.mjs`). One file in this repository's own `src/`\nwas rejected too.\n\n**Fix.** There are two parts:\n\n- `=` and `:` are no longer separators when followed by `>`. `=>` is its own separator.\n- `sanitizeCredentialText` runs to a fixed point, with at most 3 passes. A future\n  non-idempotent rule can then no longer block publication by itself.\n\n`experiments/issue-2397-fixed-point-only.mjs` shows that the fixed-point loop alone\nalready unblocks the reproducer. `experiments/issue-2397-fuzz-idempotency.mjs` fuzzes the\nproperty.\n\n### RC4b — the verifier blocked what the maskers left alone\n\nThe last residual check, `containsKnownToken`, looks for every value in\n`KNO…ARS` in the output, at any length. The maskers disagreed with it in\ntwo ways:\n\n- every masker skips values shorter than 12 characters;\n- `sanitizeOutput`, which the log path uses, only masked GitHub CLI tokens, not the env\n  tokens.\n\nAs a result:\n\n- With `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID=123456789`, the chat id is not a secret and is never\n  masked. Every log that mentions it, or any number that contains it (such as\n  `upload size 9123456789 bytes`), was blocked with `known-token:TEL…\n- A `GITHUB_PAT` that matches no vendor pattern was never masked in logs, so any log\n  that echoed it was blocked with `known-token:GIT…oth are reproduced in `experiments/issue-2397-known-token-mismatch.mjs`.\n\n**Fix.** `MIN…GTH = 12` is now shared by the maskers and the verifier, and\n`sanitizeOutput` also masks the env tokens. Publication is still fail-closed for every\nvalue that can be masked, and a value that cannot be masked no longer blocks forever.\n\n### D1 — \"publication was blocked\" gave no reason\n\n`CredentialSanitizationError` discarded its cause. \"Credential sanitization failed;\npublication was blocked.\" could therefore not tell apart:\n\n- a crash in the primary sanitizer;\n- Secretlint being unavailable;\n- a residual found by the core rules, Secretlint or the known-token scan;\n\nand it did not say where in a 5 MB log the problem was.\n\n**Fix.** The error now carries:\n\n- `stage`: `primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`;\n- `findings`: rule ids with counts, never the matched text;\n- `blockIndex`, `blockStartChar` and `blockChars`, from the streaming sanitizer;\n- all of the above across the bounded worker boundary.\n\n`describeCredentialSanitizationFailure()` renders them into the \"Last upload error\" line,\nfor example\n`Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked. (stage: residual; findings: known-token:[REDACTED]; log block 3 starting at character 2097152, 1048576 characters)`.\nThe next blocked upload will therefore name its root cause in the PR comment itself.\n\n## Comparison with other pull requests (R3)\n\n- **Normal failures report once.** For example `audio-decomposer#5` (2026-09-05): one\n  \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed\" with the log uploaded as a Gist. When the upload succeeds,\n  `attachLogToGitHub` returns `true`, the flag is set and the notifier stays quiet. The\n  three-comment pattern therefore needs a failed upload, which is why it was first seen\n  on #76.\n- **Stop and limit-reached runs reported twice.** These are the RC2b rows above. The bug\n  was older than #76 and had been going on since at least 2026-08-02.\n- **Separate sessions report separately.** For example fa49 #2 at 2026-09-27 15:05:05 and\n  15:06:09: two sessions failed, each with its own log. Each failure is real. The\n  \"latest comment\" rule keeps these reports, and a test pins that.\n\n## Same problem elsewhere (R10)\n\n- All tool comments, including stop, limit-reached, ready and failure comments, go\n  through `postTrackedComment`, so the per-target record sees all of them. The search was\n  `grep -rn \"gh pr comment\\|gh issue comment\\|/comments\" src`. The only other poster,\n  `session-kill-recovery.lib.mjs`, posts a recovery notice, not a failure report.\n- All credential masking for publication goes through\n  `credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`, so the separator and fixed-point fix applies\n  to:\n  - comments\n  - Gist and log uploads\n  - Sentry payloads\n  - the interactive-mode PR stream\n- The known-token threshold is one constant, used by `sanitizeOutput`,\n  `sanitizeCommentBody`, `maskEncodedKnownTokens` and `containsKnownToken`. That last\n  function is also behind the interactive-mode leak warning.\n\n## Upstream: openai/codex\n\nThe error text is not specific to an ended plan. openai/codex#49396 (\"Codex CLI says\ngpt-6.1-sol is unsupported with ChatGPT sign-in without explaining eligibility\") reports\nthe identical 400 from **active** Pro accounts. In the comments of 2026-09-30 and\n2026-10-01, users trace it to a background app-server daemon that is older than the model\n(for example CLI 0.159.3 with `appServerVersion: 0.158.0`).\n\nWorkarounds reported there:\n\n```sh\ncodex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes\ncodex app-server daemon restart\ncodex app-server daemon version   # expect >= 0.159.2\n# or, for one session\ncodex --no-daemon\n```\n\nRelated issues with the same message: #17642, #32036, #42944, #46304, #47333, #47784,\n#49619 and #49703 (`data/openai-codex-related-issues.json`).\n\nOur case adds a third cause behind the same text: the plan period ended. A comment on\n#49396 records this (see the PR description for the link) and suggests a fix in Codex:\nreturn distinct error codes or messages for\n\n- not entitled by plan,\n- plan expired,\n- model unknown to this client or daemon version, and\n- rollout not reached.\n\nIt also suggests that the CLI warn when its version differs from the daemon's. A new issue\nwas not filed, because #49396 is the open tracking issue for exactly this message.\n\nUntil Codex distinguishes these causes, Hive Mind lists all of them in its guidance (RC3).\n\n## Existing tools considered\n\n- **Secretlint** (already a dependency) is used as the second scanner. It does not cover\n  sanitizer idempotency, which is our own invariant.\n- **gitleaks**, **TruffleHog** and **detect-secrets** are detectors, not maskers. They\n  would add a third opinion, but not the guarantee that masking is stable. That guarantee\n  is what the publication boundary depends on, so the fix is to make masking a fixed\n  point.\n- **Sticky-comment actions** (`marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment`,\n  `peter-evans/create-or-update-comment`) solve \"one comment per purpose\" by editing a\n  marked comment. Hive Mind needs a separate comment per session for history. It\n  therefore applies the same idea in memory, as a per-target \"already reported\" record,\n  instead of editing comments.\n\n## Remaining uncertainty\n\n- The log of the affected run cannot be read from here, so it is not proven which\n  residual blocked that upload. RC4 is the most likely cause:\n  - a Codex session that reads JavaScript sources prints arrow functions;\n  - one such file in 340 was blocked in our own corpus scan.\n  - RC4b applies only if the solver host has `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID` or a custom\n    `GITHUB_PAT` set.\n- Both are fixed. If an upload is still blocked, the PR comment will now name the stage,\n  rule id and log block (D1), and running\n  `gh-upload-log /home/box/solve-2026-09-30T14-55-22-906Z.log` on the host will show the\n  same information.\n\n## Reproducing\n\n```sh\nnode experiments/issue-2397-replay-three-comments.mjs     # three comments before the fix, one after\nnode experiments/issue-2397-min-repro.mjs                 # 'token =[REDACTED]' bl…`\n"

Every log that mentions it, or any number that contains it (such as\n  `upload size 9123456789 bytes`), was blocked with `known-token:TEL…\n- A `GITHUB_PAT` that matches no vendor pattern was never masked in logs, so any log\n  that echoed it was blocked with `known-token:GIT…oth are reproduced in `experiments/issue-2397-known-token-mismatch.mjs`.\n\n**Fix.** `MIN…GTH = 12` is now shared by the maskers and the verifier, and\n`sanitizeOutput` also masks the env tokens. Publication is still fail-closed for every\nvalue that can be masked, and a value that cannot be masked no longer blocks forever.\n\n### D1 — \"publication was blocked\" gave no reason\n\n`CredentialSanitizationError` discarded its cause. \"Credential sanitization failed;\npublication was blocked.\" could therefore not tell apart:\n\n- a crash in the primary sanitizer;\n- Secretlint being unavailable;\n- a residual found by the core rules, Secretlint or the known-token scan;\n\nand it did not say where in a 5 MB log the problem was.\n\n**Fix.** The error now carries:\n\n- `stage`: `primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`;\n- `findings`: rule ids with counts, never the matched text;\n- `blockIndex`, `blockStartChar` and `blockChars`, from the streaming sanitizer;\n- all of the above across the bounded worker boundary.\n\n`describeCredentialSanitizationFailure()` renders them into the \"Last upload error\" line,\nfor example\n`Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked. (stage: residual; findings: known-token:[REDACTED]; log block 3 starting at character 2097152, 1048576 characters)`.\nThe next blocked upload will therefore name its root cause in the PR comment itself.\n\n## Comparison with other pull requests (R3)\n\n- **Normal failures report once.** For example `audio-decomposer#5` (2026-09-05): one\n  \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed\" with the log uploaded as a Gist. When the upload succeeds,\n  `attachLogToGitHub` returns `true`, the flag is set and the notifier stays quiet. The\n  three-comment pattern therefore needs a failed upload, which is why it was first seen\n  on #76.\n- **Stop and limit-reached runs reported twice.** These are the RC2b rows above. The bug\n  was older than #76 and had been going on since at least 2026-08-02.\n- **Separate sessions report separately.** For example fa49 #2 at 2026-09-27 15:05:05 and\n  15:06:09: two sessions failed, each with its own log. Each failure is real. The\n  \"latest comment\" rule keeps these reports, and a test pins that.\n\n## Same problem elsewhere (R10)\n\n- All tool comments, including stop, limit-reached, ready and failure comments, go\n  through `postTrackedComment`, so the per-target record sees all of them. The search was\n  `grep -rn \"gh pr comment\\|gh issue comment\\|/comments\" src`. The only other poster,\n  `session-kill-recovery.lib.mjs`, posts a recovery notice, not a failure report.\n- All credential masking for publication goes through\n  `credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`, so the separator and fixed-point fix applies\n  to:\n  - comments\n  - Gist and log uploads\n  - Sentry payloads\n  - the interactive-mode PR stream\n- The known-token threshold is one constant, used by `sanitizeOutput`,\n  `sanitizeCommentBody`, `maskEncodedKnownTokens` and `containsKnownToken`. That last\n  function is also behind the interactive-mode leak warning.\n\n## Upstream: openai/codex\n\nThe error text is not specific to an ended plan. openai/codex#49396 (\"Codex CLI says\ngpt-6.1-sol is unsupported with ChatGPT sign-in without explaining eligibility\") reports\nthe identical 400 from **active** Pro accounts. A new issue\nwas not filed, because #49396 is the open tracking issue for exactly this message.\n\nUntil Codex distinguishes these causes, Hive Mind lists all of them in its guidance (RC3).\n\n## Existing tools considered\n\n- **Secretlint** (already a dependency) is used as the second scanner. It does not cover\n  sanitizer idempotency, which is our own invariant.\n- **gitleaks**, **TruffleHog** and **detect-secrets** are detectors, not maskers. The fix:\n  - `=` and `:` no longer match as separators before `>`;\n  - the sanitizer runs to a bounded fixed point, so a future rule that is not idempotent cannot block publication on its own.\n- **RC4b:** `containsKnownToken` checked env values of any length, while the maskers only mask values of 12+ characters, and the log masker ignored env tokens. It adds the stage (`primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`), the rule ids with counts, and the log block index and position. These details also cross the bounded-worker boundary. None of them said that the plan had to be renewed, and the log upload was blocked with no reason given. This PR fixes each root cause and adds a reproducing test for each one. Every test failed before its fix.\n\nFull case study: [`docs/case-studies/issue-2397/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2397-36ba658228ab/docs/case-studies/issue-2397/README.md). It covers the timeline, the requirements, the evidence, a comparison with other PRs, the upstream report and the remaining uncertainty.\n\n### One failure comment\n\n- **RC1:** `attachLogToGitHub` posts a \"Log Upload Failed\" failure report and then returns `false`. The exit-handler notifier therefore reported the failure again. `postTrackedComment` now records the latest tool comment per PR or issue, and the notifier skips a target that already carries a failure report.\n- **RC2:** after that upload failure, the notifier also posted its own fallback comment, which was the third one. It no longer does when the upload already posted the report.\n- **RC2b:** comparable PRs (`test-hello-world-…fa49#2` and `…00e1#2`, since 2026-08-02) showed the same doubling after `🛑 Automation stopped` and `❌ Auto-restart N/N - limit reached`. These two comments now count as the failure report for the rest of the run, including when `✅ Ready to merge` is posted after them.\n- Separate sessions that each fail still get one report each, because the check looks at the latest comment, not at any earlier comment.\n\n### Clear reason\n\n- **RC3:** `The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.` is now classified as a Codex `PLAN_RESTRICTED` error. The guidance tells the user to:\n  - renew the plan (with a link to the plan page),\n  - choose a model with `--model`,\n  - run `codex login` again, and\n  - run `codex app-server daemon update`, because a stale daemon returns the same 400 on an active plan ([openai/codex#49396](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49396)).\n\n### Log upload\n\n- **RC4:** the credential sanitizer was not idempotent for `token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED], which the second pass turned into `token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED]`. The publication boundary treats \"a second pass would change the text\" as a leaked credential. As a result, any log containing such an arrow function, or a Ruby/PHP `'password' =[REDACTED] [REDACTED], was blocked; that is 23 of 8492 files in `node_modules`. The fix:\n  - `=` and `:` no longer match as separators before `>`;\n  - the sanitizer runs to a bounded fixed point, so a future rule that is not idempotent cannot block publication on its own.\n- **RC4b:** `containsKnownToken` checked env values of any length, while the maskers only mask values of 12+ characters, and the log masker ignored env tokens. As a result:\n  - `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID=123456789` blocked every log that mentioned it;\n  - a `GITHUB_PAT` with no vendor shape was never masked in logs and blocked publication.\n\n  The fix shares one `MIN…GTH` between the maskers and the verifier, and `sanitizeOutput` now masks env tokens too.\n- **D1, diagnostics:** \"Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked.\" now says which check blocked the upload. It adds the stage (`primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`), the rule ids with counts, and the log block index and position. These details also cross the bounded-worker boundary. ## Summary

Fixes #2397.

When the ChatGPT Pro plan ended during a Codex run on konard/vietnam-accomodation-search#76, Hive Mind posted **three** "🚨 Solution Draft Failed" comments within five seconds. None of them said that the plan had to be renewed, and the log upload was blocked with no reason given. This PR fixes each root cause and adds a reproducing test for each one. Every test failed before its fix.

Full case study: [`docs/case-studies/issue-2397/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2397-36ba658228ab/docs/case-studies/issue-2397/README.md). It covers the timeline, the requirements, the evidence, a comparison with other PRs, the upstream report and the remaining uncertainty.

### One failure comment

- **RC1:** `attachLogToGitHub` posts a "Log Upload Failed" failure report and then returns `false`. The exit-handler notifier therefore reported the failure again. `postTrackedComment` now records the latest tool comment per PR or issue, and the notifier skips a target that already carries a failure report.
- **RC2:** after that upload failure, the notifier also posted its own fallback comment, which was the third one. It no longer does when the upload already posted the report.
- **RC2b:** comparable PRs (`test-hello-world-…fa49#2` and `…00e1#2`, since 2026-08-02) showed the same doubling after `🛑 Automation stopped` and `❌ Auto-restart N/N - limit reached`. These two comments now count as the failure report for the rest of the run, including when `✅ Ready to merge` is posted after them.
- Separate sessions that each fail still get one report each, because the check looks at the latest comment, not at any earlier comment.

### Clear reason

- **RC3:** `The '<model>' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.` is now classified as a Codex `PLAN_RESTRICTED` error. The guidance tells the user to:
  - renew the plan (with a link to the plan page),
  - choose a model with `--model`,
  - run `codex login` again, and
  - run `codex app-server daemon update`, because a stale daemon returns the same 400 on an active plan ([openai/codex#49396](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49396)).

### Log upload

- **RC4:** the credential sanitizer was not idempotent for `token => [REDACTED], which the second pass turned into `token =[REDACTED] [REDACTED]`. The publication boundary treats "a second pass would change the text" as a leaked credential. As a result, any log containing such an arrow function, or a Ruby/PHP `'password' => [REDACTED], was blocked; that is 23 of 8492 files in `node_modules`. The fix:
  - `=` and `:` no longer match as separators before `>`;
  - the sanitizer runs to a bounded fixed point, so a future rule that is not idempotent cannot block publication on its own.
- **RC4b:** `containsKnownToken` checked env values of any length, while the maskers only mask values of 12+ characters, and the log masker ignored env tokens. As a result:
  - `TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID=123456789` blocked every log that mentioned it;
  - a `GITHUB_PAT` with no vendor shape was never masked in logs and blocked publication.

  The fix shares one `MIN…GTH` between the maskers and the verifier, and `sanitizeOutput` now masks env tokens too.
- **D1, diagnostics:** "Credential sanitization failed; publication was blocked." now says which check blocked the upload. It adds the stage (`primary`, `residual-scan`, `secretlint`, `known-token-scan` or `residual`), the rule ids with counts, and the log block index and position. These details also cross the bounded-worker boundary. Matched text is never included.

### Upstream

- Commented on openai/codex#49396 ([comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49396#issuecomment-5933238726)). The comment:
  - reports the plan-expired case behind the same message;
  - lists the workarounds for each cause;
  - suggests distinct error codes for each cause, plus a warning when the CLI and daemon versions differ.
- I did not open a new issue, because #49396 already tracks this exact message.

### CI

CI on this branch failed twice for reasons unrelated to the fix:

- stale dependency pins plus the brace-expansion advisory;
- the freshness gate demanding `rust:1.99-slim-bookworm`, an image Docker Hub had not published yet.

I fixed both here, but main fixed the same two problems at the same time (ef33600b and 395afb3f, from #2396). The merge therefore takes main's versions, and this PR's net diff contains only the #2397 changes.

## How to reproduce

```sh
node experiments/issue-2397-replay-three-comments.mjs   # 3 comments before, 1 after
node experiments/issue-2397-min-repro.mjs               # 'token =[REDACTED]' blocked before
node experiments/issue-2397-known-token-mismatch.mjs    # short env value blocked before
```

## Tests

- `tests/issue-2397-single-failure-comment.test.mjs` (11 tests): replays #76, the stop, limit-reached and Ready-to-merge sequences, and the fallback cases.
- `tests/issue-2397-codex-plan-restricted.test.mjs` (6 tests).
- `tests/issue-2397-sanitizer-idempotency.test.mjs` (11 tests).
- `tests/issue-2397-known-token-consistency.test.mjs` (5 tests).
- `tests/issue-2397-sanitization-failure-diagnostics.test.mjs` (6 tests).
- Existing sanitization, comment, notifier and subscription suites (46 files) still pass.
- `tests/test-solution-summary.mjs` fails with `checkForAiCreatedComments should be imported`. It fails the same way on `main`, so this PR did not cause it.
- `lint`, `format:check`, `check:duplication` and `check:secrets` pass.

## Remaining uncertainty

The log of the affected run was never published; it is still on the host that ran the session. So it is not proven which residual blocked that particular upload. RC4 is the most likely cause, since Codex streams the JavaScript files it reads into the log. Both candidate causes are fixed. If an upload is blocked again, D1 will name the check in the PR comment itself.
